conclusion: On clean labels (outlier_fraction 0.0, task_version 1), OLS shows lower error than the matched training-mean baseline across all three executed seeds (7, 19, 31) and all three metrics (mse, mae, median_absolute_error). For mse, linear ranges 0.12035336475545051-0.17046895861013783 vs baseline 11.274002085630377-13.77357566104946; for mae, linear 0.26707244487817117-0.31271792820150346 vs baseline 2.866191572807901-3.171599457525345; for median_absolute_error, linear 0.19880194230096437-0.25288422842521774 vs baseline 2.701903458261778-3.1412061139149094. The direction is consistent across seeds and metrics, but this is a bounded synthetic regression study and no general scientific value is claimed.
limitations: Only three seeds (7, 19, 31) were executed; no broader seed sampling or seed-variance estimate beyond these three.
Only three metrics (mse, mae, median_absolute_error) were computed; other metrics are uncharacterized.
No uncertainty quantification, confidence intervals, or statistical tests comparing linear vs baseline were performed.
No independent verification was performed; numbers are copied from the artifacts and sha256 values are recorded but not independently checked.
Results are conditioned on task_version 1 and outlier_fraction 0.0 (clean labels) only; behavior on other conditions is unknown.
The large baseline errors relative to linear may reflect the matched-baseline construction rather than model quality; the baseline definition was not inspected.
No claim of general scientific value is made.
